picks.analysis: Lamar Jackson has been ruled out and Baltimore is expected to rest multiple established starters, shifting the personnel advantage decisively to Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts has been sharp in camp building chemistry with Elijah Moore, while the Eagles continue to emphasize their run game and tush push package — a physical identity that dominates when the opposing defense is running backup personnel. Philadelphia's defensive front, led by a dominant Moro Ojomo whose camp intensity has been generating headlines, should impose their will against Baltimore's inexperienced second-unit offensive line. Eagles -3.5 is the clearest value on the board this week.

With Josh Allen and the Bills' starters set to play in their first game at the new stadium, expect a focused performance. The Bills' offensive line has shown strong cohesion in camp, which will be crucial against a Panthers front missing Nic Scourton due to injury. The continuity in Buffalo's starting lineup gives them an edge in this matchup.

Seattle's secondary rotation has been a standout in camp, with Devon Witherspoon emerging as a potential starter. The Cowboys' offense, led by Dak Prescott, has struggled with consistency in practice, particularly against aggressive secondaries. Seattle's defensive depth could exploit these issues, especially at home.

Miami's training camp has highlighted Malik Willis's leadership in the offense, which could spell trouble for Washington's defense still adjusting under new schemes. The Dolphins' receiving corps has been dynamic, with De'Von Achane showcasing his speed, likely creating mismatches against Washington's secondary.

Daniel Jones's return has bolstered the Colts' offense, with the QB showing no signs of last season's injury. The Patriots' defense has struggled to contain mobile quarterbacks in camp, and Jones's dual-threat ability could be a decisive factor. Expect the Colts to capitalize on this matchup advantage.
